title: Post-Quantum P2P for Ethereum: Inventory and Per-Component Migration Plan
description: Most post-quantum work in Ethereum focuses on signatures and accounts, but the consensus-layer networking stack has its own quantum exposure. I start with an inventory of the P2P layer: node identity in discv5 ENRs and libp2p peer IDs (secp256k1 keys), the discv5 session handshake, Noise over TCP and TLS 1.3 over QUIC for transport security, and the symmetric ciphers and hashes underneath. For each component I classify the threat (harvest-now-decrypt-later versus future impersonation), then propose a migration path: hybrid ML-KEM key exchange for the handshakes, and new identity schemes for ENRs and peer IDs, where PQ keys and signatures do not fit within the 300-byte ENR limit. I close with the order I would migrate things in and the open questions for client and libp2p teams.
